title: Fake Medicare Calls Threaten to Cancel Coverage
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare and claim your coverage will be canceled unless you give personal information or pay a fee. They may use scare tactics to pressure you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your coverage will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and pay a reactivation fee right now."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security number or banking info
Threatens to cancel your Medicare coverage
Demands immediate payment or personal details
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Text Message Package Delivery Scam
how_it_works: You get a text saying a package couldn’t be delivered and you need to click a link to reschedule. The link leads to a fake website that tries to steal your personal or payment information.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please confirm your address by clicking here: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link to a website you don’t recognize
Requests for payment or personal info to release a package
what_to_do: Do not click the link. Contact the delivery company using their official website or phone number.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails pretending to be from the Social Security Administration. They say there is a problem with your account and ask you to click a link or call a number, trying to steal your information.
example_message: "We have detected suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please verify your information immediately by clicking this link."
red_flags: Email claims to be urgent or threatening
Asks you to click a link or download an attachment
Comes from an unusual or misspelled email address
what_to_do: Delete the email. If you’re worried, call Social Security at their official number.

title: Romance Scam on Facebook
how_it_works: Someone you meet on Facebook quickly wants to move your conversation to private messages. They share a sad story and ask for money, pretending to be in love or in trouble.
example_message: "I care about you so much, but I need your help. My bank account is frozen and I can’t buy food. Can you send me some money?"
red_flags: Person you’ve never met asks for money
Wants to move the chat off Facebook
Shares a dramatic or urgent story
what_to_do: Stop communicating and never send money to someone you haven’t met in person.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: You get a call from someone pretending to be your grandchild or a police officer. They say your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away for bail or an emergency.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in jail and need money for bail. Please don’t tell Mom and Dad. Can you send $2,000 right now?"
red_flags: Wants money sent by wire transfer or gift cards
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member directly to check the story.
